title: Warm pools and Spot
bridge: A warm pool is like keeping browser tabs open but asleep: waking one is fast, and a sleeping tab costs almost nothing. Except a used VM never goes back to the pool; it is thrown away. Spot is like a standby airline seat: much cheaper, but AWS can take it back with two minutes' warning.
intro: A run should get its VM in about a minute, and a VM waiting on a person should cost cents. This lesson shows the AWS pieces behind that. Auto Scaling groups keep warm pools of stopped VMs. A lifecycle hook finishes setup before a VM sleeps. Spot groups run cheap work that can retry.

picture.caption: Warm VMs are prepared once and stopped; a claim wakes one and takes it out of the group for good.

steps.text: launches VMs for the pool from the launch template
each new VM waits in the hook while sandbox-warm starts FCP Lab once
CONTINUE: the VM is stopped and kept, costing only its disk
a warm VM starts in about a minute, turns InService, and is detached
routines only: AWS may reclaim a Spot VM; spot-watch sees the notice and the run checkpoints

p: A fresh VM must boot, pull Docker images and start FCP Lab before a run can begin. That takes many minutes. A VM that did all that once and was then stopped wakes in about a minute.

A stopped VM costs only its disk, about $8 to $10 a month (G3-15). A running full VM costs about $0.42 an hour; parked, about $0.01 (G3-20). So we keep a few VMs stopped and ready: 2 lite, 2 full and 0 wide to start.

callout.text: Warm pools turn a slow, identical start into work done once, before anyone is waiting. The run then spends its time on the ticket.

sections.h: Auto Scaling group: a count AWS keeps true
p: An Auto Scaling group (ASG) keeps a number of VMs running from one launch template, in the subnets you give it. That number is the desired capacity. Raise it and AWS starts a VM; lower it and AWS removes one.
Our groups have min 0, max 3 and desired 0 (G3-15). Nothing is in service until a run claims a VM. The max only covers claims in flight, because claimed VMs leave the group.
sections.because: We create the group with desired 0 because the steady state is 'all VMs warm and stopped', not 'some running'.

code.text:
aws ec2 create-launch-template --launch-template-name lab-full \
  --launch-template-data '{"ImageId":"ami-03cf127a","InstanceType":"m8i.2xlarge"}'
SUB=$(aws ec2 describe-subnets --query 'Subnets[0].SubnetId' --output text)
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name ai-agents-sandbox-full \
  --launch-template 'LaunchTemplateName=lab-full,Version=$Latest' \
  --min-size 0 --max-size 3 --desired-capacity 0 --vpc-zone-identifier $SUB

notes.text: A small template for the lab. The real ones are the p3-3 templates.
Any subnet works in moto. In the account, the group spans the three sandbox subnets.
$Latest: new VMs use the newest template version. Single quotes stop the shell expanding $Latest.
min 0, max 3, desired 0, as in G3-15.

p: A warm pool is a set of prepared VMs kept next to the group, outside its desired capacity. With pool state Stopped, they are shut down and cost only disk.

A pool VM moves through states: Warmed:Pending, then Warmed:Pending:Wait while a hook runs, then Warmed:Stopped. On a scale-out it becomes Pending, then InService. G3-15 sets reuse_on_scale_in to false: a VM that served a run is never put back.
sections.because: We forbid reuse because a used VM may hold a run's leftovers, and one fresh VM per run is a wall.

code.text:
aws autoscaling put-warm-pool --auto-scaling-group-name ai-agents-sandbox-full \
  --pool-state Stopped --min-size 2 --max-group-prepared-capacity 2 \
  --instance-reuse-policy ReuseOnScaleIn=false
aws autoscaling describe-warm-pool --auto-scaling-group-name ai-agents-sandbox-full

notes.text: Stopped VMs, at least 2. max-group-prepared-capacity caps the pool plus the group at 2.
Used VMs are terminated on scale-in, never returned to the pool.
On AWS, Instances lists the pool VMs with their LifecycleState. moto stores the settings but starts no VMs.

sections.h: The lifecycle hook: finish setup, then sleep
p: A lifecycle hook pauses a VM at a transition until someone says 'continue'. G3-15 adds one on launch: heartbeat 1800 seconds, default ABANDON. If the VM does not finish within 30 minutes, AWS throws it away instead of keeping a half-ready VM.

The image has a sandbox-warm systemd unit (p3-5) that runs at boot as root. It asks IMDS where this VM is going. For Warmed:Stopped it starts FCP Lab once, to pull images and warm the disk, stops it, and completes the hook. For InService it completes at once.
sections.because: We let the VM finish setup before it sleeps, because work done in the pool is work no run waits for.

code.file: sandbox-warm (sketch; a systemd unit in the image role, G3-15)
code.text:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
imds() {  # IMDSv2 read, as in p3-3
  local t; t=$(curl -s -X PUT http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 60")
  curl -s -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $t" "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/$1"
}
id=$(imds instance-id)
target=$(imds autoscaling/target-lifecycle-state)   # Warmed:Stopped or InService
group=$(cat /etc/ai-agent-sandbox/asg-name)         # how the VM learns its group: settle in G3-15
if [ "$target" = "Warmed:Stopped" ]; then
  sudo -iu agent lab start sandbox && sudo -iu agent lab stop sandbox   # pull images, warm the disk
fi
aws autoscaling complete-lifecycle-action --lifecycle-hook-name finish-setup \
  --auto-scaling-group-name "$group" --instance-id "$id" --lifecycle-action-result CONTINUE

notes.text: The VM's destination. Only root can read it, because of the p3-3 host rules.
The group name is not in IMDS (metadata tags are off). The ticket does not say how the VM learns it.
Check the lab command with Nave: G3-16 uses lab start, G3-14 uses lab up.
Uses the role's one extra permission (p3-1) through the autoscaling endpoint (p3-2).
CONTINUE moves the VM on: into the pool (stopped) or into service.

sections.h: Claiming a VM: scale out, then detach
p: To claim a VM, the acquireSandbox activity (G3-18) raises desired capacity by 1. AWS wakes a warm VM, which turns InService. The activity then detaches it with ShouldDecrementDesiredCapacity, which puts the count back to 0.

After that the VM is no longer in the group. The ASG will not replace or terminate it; Temporal owns its life. The activity tags it with the run ID and a lease, and keeps renewing the lease while the run lives (p3-7).
sections.because: We detach claimed VMs because an ASG that still counts them might replace or remove them in the middle of a run.

notes.text: One more than now. Two claims at once each add one.
Do not wait for a cooldown period between changes.
Detach takes the VM out of the group. If two claims race for one VM, the loser's detach fails and it takes the next.
Without the decrement, the group would start another VM to get back to 1.
From here on the tags are how everyone, including the sweeper, knows whose VM this is.

sections.h: Spot: cheap, with a two-minute warning
p: Spot VMs use AWS's spare capacity, about 56% cheaper (G3-15). AWS may take one back at any time, with a notice two minutes before. G3-15 adds Spot groups for lite and full, with no warm pool.

A mixed instances policy lets the group pick from several types of the same size, so it finds spare capacity more often. Nova and the bug fixers stay on on-demand groups. They wait on people, and losing a VM mid-conversation costs more than the discount.
sections.because: We allow three instance families because a Spot group that accepts only one type often finds none.

notes.text: Same size (8 vCPU, 32 GiB), three generations. Any of them can run a full sandbox.
No on-demand VMs at all in this group: 0% above a base of 0.
Pick the pools with spare capacity first, then the cheapest among them.

p: The Spot notice appears in IMDS at /latest/meta-data/spot/instance-action. Before a notice it answers 404. G3-08 adds spot-watch, a root timer that checks every 5 seconds and writes /run/nova/preempt once.

The harness sees the file, checkpoints (pushes the branch and saves the session) and exits with 'preempted'. The workflow then retries the step on a fresh VM from the same group (G3-20). Two minutes is enough for a checkpoint, not for finishing the work.
sections.because: We poll from a tiny root script because only root may reach IMDS, and the harness runs as agent.

code.file: spot-watch.sh (G3-08; IMDS and OUT can be changed for the lab)

notes.text: The real address by default. The lab points it at a fake server on your laptop.
Already warned: nothing to do. The harness reads this file.
-f makes curl fail on 404, so 'no notice yet' exits quietly.
The notice is JSON: the action (terminate or stop) and the time it happens.

quiz.q: Why does the warm pool set reuse_on_scale_in to false?

options.text: Stopped VMs that were used cost more than new ones
options.why: Price is the same. The reason is what a used VM may still hold.

options.text: A used VM may hold a run's leftovers, so it is never put back for the next run
options.why: One fresh VM per run is a wall; reuse would break it.

options.text: AWS requires it for pools in the Stopped state
options.why: It is a choice. AWS allows reuse; we turn it off.

quiz.q: Why is a claimed VM detached from its group?

options.text: Detached VMs are billed at a lower rate
So the warm pool shrinks for good
options.why: The pool refills to its min size; detaching does not shrink it.

options.text: So the ASG never replaces or terminates it; Temporal owns its life from then on
options.why: And with the decrement, the group's desired capacity goes back to 0.

quiz.q: Which work runs on the Spot groups?

options.text: Routines that can retry, such as CI fixers; never Nova, which waits on people
options.why: A lost Spot VM costs a retry. For a run waiting on a person, that is too disruptive.

options.text: Everything, since Spot is about 56% cheaper
options.why: Nova and bug fixers stay on on-demand groups on purpose.

options.text: Only wide VMs, because they cost the most
options.why: G3-15 makes Spot groups for lite and full, by kind of work, not by size.

words.plain: A group that keeps a count of VMs running from one launch template in given subnets.
The count an ASG keeps true; raise it to start a VM, lower it to remove one.
Prepared VMs kept next to an ASG, ours stopped, ready to join it in about a minute.
A pause at a VM's transition until someone completes it, or a timeout applies the default result.
Take a VM out of its ASG so the group no longer counts, replaces or removes it.
A VM on AWS's spare capacity, much cheaper, that AWS may take back.
The two-minute warning a Spot VM gets in IMDS at spot/instance-action.

tickets.why: One ASG per size with a stopped warm pool, the finish-setup hook, no reuse, and Spot groups for routines.
acquireSandbox raises desired by one, waits for InService, detaches with decrement and tags the VM.
On a Spot notice the harness checkpoints and exits preempted; the workflow retries on a fresh VM.
The image's spot-watch timer polls the notice every 5 seconds and writes /run/nova/preempt.

remember: Keep VMs stopped and ready, claim one by scaling out and detaching it, and never put it back. Spot is for retryable work only.
